visual-d6d3a6d5b53f677ef38a.title: Effect of Exchange‑Rate Movements
rows: When the exchange rate goes up, it means the local currency (e.g., the dollar) appreciates, i.e., you get more foreign currency per unit of domestic currency.
When the exchange rate goes down, it indicates a depreciation of the local currency.

visual-f8eb31096bfabada14a6.title: Interest‑Rate Channels by Economy Type
rows: In a closed economy the interest‑rate channel operated only through reduced investment.
In an open economy a second channel appears: a higher interest rate raises the exchange rate, making exports more expensive and imports cheaper, so net exports fall.
